postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:40 — [P1, confidence 100] `if SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?; Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` couples each previously unseen embed URL to a synchronous full-feed scan, so loading N distinct uncached article embeds downloads and reparses the same N-item feed N times (O(N²) work) before falling back to the individual article.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a performance issue in lib/topic_retriever.rb. Looking at lines 37-42 in perform_retrieve, when feed_polling_enabled is true, it calls Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously for each uncached embed URL. The PollFeed job (in app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb) downloads and parses the entire RSS feed. If N distinct uncached URLs are requested, this results in downloading and parsing the same feed N times before the individual fetch_http fallback. This is O(N²) work as described - a real performance/correctness issue where the same expensive operation is repeated unnecessarily.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:15 — [P1, confidence 75] `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` treats the caller’s raw URL string as article identity across lookup, storage, and import, so equivalent forms such as an added fragment, default port, or trailing slash create separate topics for the same article and defeat deduplication; although exact-string identity is simple, canonicalizing once deletes the duplicated normalization burden from every producer and lookup.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that TopicEmbed.import uses exact URL string matching via `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` without any URL normalization. This means URLs like 'http://example.com/page' and 'http://example.com/page/' or 'http://example.com/page#section' would be treated as different articles, potentially creating duplicate topics. This is visible in the diff at lines 15-17 of topic_embed.rb. While this is a legitimate design concern about URL canonicalization, it's not strictly a bug - the code works as written, just with a limitation. It's an architectural/design consideration that could lead to duplicate content but isn't a defect per se.

This is verifiable in the diff at db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb. However, this is not a bug per se - it's a design decision common in Rails applications where referential integrity is handled at the application level. The concern about orphaned records is valid but speculative - the application code in TopicEmbed.import shows proper handling within transactions. This is more of an architectural concern/best practice suggestion rather than a concrete bug that will cause immediate issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — P1/confidence 100: `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false` backfills every existing post with enum value 1 (`raw_html`), so all historical posts bypass the cooking pipeline and return their raw source as trusted cooked HTML after deployment.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `cook_method` with `default: 1`. Looking at the Post model in the diff, `Post.cook_methods` is defined as `Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`, which means `:regular` = 1 and `:raw_html` = 2 (Enum starts at 1). The `cook` method checks `if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` to skip cooking. Since default is 1 (`:regular`), existing posts will still go through normal cooking. The finding incorrectly states that value 1 is `raw_html` - it's actually `:regular`. This is a misreading of how the Enum works.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — P1/confidence 100: `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` makes replaying this already-shipped migration drop the populated `top_topics` table before recreating it, irreversibly deleting all accumulated topic-ranking data.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `create_table :top_topics, force: true` in db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb. The `force: true` option drops the table if it exists before creating it. For a migration that has already been shipped and run in production, if this migration is ever re-run (e.g., during certain database operations or if someone manually runs it), it would drop the existing `top_topics` table and all its data. This is a real data loss risk. The finding correctly identifies this as a problem - migrations should not use `force: true` as it can cause irreversible data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — [P1, confidence 100] `open(url).read` performs a timeout-less, unbounded download in the embed retrieval worker, so a stalled origin pins a worker indefinitely and a large response exhausts worker memory while the iframe remains on its loading loop.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in app/models/topic_embed.rb line 48: `doc = Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`. This uses Ruby's `open-uri` to fetch a remote URL without any timeout configuration or size limits. The finding correctly identifies that: 1) A slow/stalled origin server would block the worker indefinitely since there's no timeout, 2) A large response would be fully loaded into memory before processing, potentially exhausting worker memory. This is called from TopicRetriever.fetch_http and Jobs::RetrieveTopic, which are background workers. The vulnerability is real and verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 — [P1, confidence 100] `rss = SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` performs a timeout-less, unbounded feed download, so a stalled or oversized feed pins or exhausts the scheduled worker and `sidekiq_options retry: false` leaves the entire polling interval unprocessed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` being called without any timeout configuration. The `open-uri` library in Ruby by default has no timeout, meaning a slow or malicious feed server could cause the worker to hang indefinitely. Combined with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, if the job hangs or fails, it won't be retried, leaving the polling interval unprocessed. This is a real defect in the new code - network operations should have timeouts to prevent resource exhaustion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:27 — [P2, confidence 100] `if $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` commits the deduplication key before retrieval succeeds, so any downstream exception makes the next iframe reload skip recovery and falsely remain in the loading state until the key expires.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a race condition in lib/topic_retriever.rb. Looking at lines 25-31, the code sets the Redis key with `setnx` and `expire` BEFORE calling `perform_retrieve`. If `perform_retrieve` fails (e.g., network error, parsing error in `fetch_http` or `TopicEmbed.import_remote`), the key remains set for 60 seconds, causing subsequent requests to return early from `retrieved_recently?` without attempting retrieval. This means the embed iframe would stay in 'loading' state until the key expires, which is a real bug in the error recovery path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:49 — [P1, confidence 100] `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` raises NoMethodError when `embed_by_username` is blank, so a valid embed request under the default configuration repeatedly displays “loading” while every retrieval job fails.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is correct. In lib/topic_retriever.rb line 49, the code calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without checking if `embed_by_username` is blank first. Looking at config/site_settings.yml, the default value for `embed_by_username` is an empty string `''`. When `embed_by_username` is blank (empty string), calling `.downcase` on it won't fail, but the `User.where(username_lower: '').first` will return nil, and then the method returns early. However, the real issue is that when `embed_by_username` is nil (not just empty string), calling `.downcase` on nil would raise NoMethodError. The site setting defaults to empty string, so the immediate crash scenario requires nil specifically. But the finding correctly identifies that with default configuration (empty string), the user lookup will fail to find anyone, causing the retrieval to silently fail and the loading state to persist. This is a valid bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 — [P1, confidence 75] `revisor.revise!(user, absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true)` ignores a false revision result and line 37 still advances `content_sha1`, so a failed post update is recorded as current and will never be retried until the remote content changes again.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in app/models/topic_embed.rb lines 30-37, the code calls `revisor.revise!()` but doesn't check its return value. The `revise!` method can return false (as seen in lib/post_revisor.rb line 14: `return false if not should_revise?`). Regardless of whether the revision succeeds, line 37 (`embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)`) always executes, updating the content_sha1 hash. This means if the revision fails for any reason, the embed record will be marked as having the new content hash even though the post wasn't actually updated. Future import attempts with the same content won't retry the update because the sha1 will match.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — P1 confidence 100: the unrelated `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|` expansion is not traceable to embed URL handling and drops an existing `top_topics` table whenever this historical migration is rerun, destroying production ranking data.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims adding 'force: true' to create_table is dangerous because it drops existing tables. However, looking at the diff, this is a migration file (20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb) that creates a new table. The 'force: true' option only matters if the table already exists when the migration runs. For a properly managed Rails application, migrations run once and are tracked - this migration would only run on fresh installs or databases that haven't run it yet. The change from no 'force' to 'force: true' in a historical migration is essentially a no-op for existing production databases that have already run this migration. Additionally, this change appears unrelated to the main embedding feature and is likely just a minor cleanup or consistency change.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a security issue. In poll_feed.rb lines 31-34, RSS content is fetched and passed to TopicEmbed.import(). In post.rb lines 131-133, when cook_method is raw_html, the raw content is returned directly without sanitization ('return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]'). While the feed URL is admin-configured, the feed contents themselves come from an external source that could be compromised or malicious, creating a stored XSS vulnerability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:48 — P1 confidence 75: `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read,` follows redirects and resolves DNS only after `TopicRetriever` compares the initial URL's hostname, so an allowed host that redirects to an internal HTTP service or resolves via DNS rebinding makes the server fetch private network and cloud-metadata endpoints; although the initial hostname equals `embeddable_host`, no redirect target or resolved address is constrained.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real SSRF vulnerability. Looking at the diff: TopicRetriever.invalid_host? only checks the initial URL's hostname against embeddable_host, but then fetch_http calls TopicEmbed.import_remote which uses open(url).read. The open-uri library follows HTTP redirects automatically, so an attacker could set up an allowed host that redirects to internal services (169.254.169.254 for cloud metadata, internal IPs, etc.). The hostname validation happens before the actual HTTP request, which can follow redirects to arbitrary destinations. This is a legitimate SSRF vulnerability in the new embedding feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 — P1 confidence 100: `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` asserts a synchronous collaborator that `EmbedController#best` never invokes because production calls `Jobs.enqueue`, so this success-path spec fails immediately and cannot validate the newly implemented asynchronous retrieval response.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, EmbedController#best (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb lines 8-18) shows that when topic_id is nil, it calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` - an asynchronous job enqueue. However, the test at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:43 sets up `TopicRetriever.expects(:new).returns(retriever)` expecting TopicRetriever to be instantiated directly in the controller.
